title: Constant sheaves on a normal scheme and the generic point
statement:
Let $Y$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] which is normal (the local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ at every point is a normal domain [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]), with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K=\kappa(\eta)=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ be the canonical morphism with image $\eta$. Let $E$ be a finite abelian group, and for a scheme $T$ let $\underline E_T$ be the constant sheaf with value $E$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with $\iota_T:E\to\underline E_T(T)$ its constant sections. For a morphism $f:Z\to Y$ let $c_f:\underline E_Y\to f_*\underline E_Z$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] be the canonical map, i.e. the unique morphism with $c_f(Y)\circ\iota_Y=\iota_Z:E\to\underline E_Z(Z)=(f_*\underline E_Z)(Y)$ [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections]; equivalently $c_f=f_*(\gamma_f)\circ\eta_f$ with $\eta_f:\underline E_Y\to f_*f^{-1}\underline E_Y$ the unit of $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $\gamma_f:f^{-1}\underline E_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline E_Z$ the canonical isomorphism [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Then:

1. $c_g:\underline E_Y\to g_*\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ is an isomorphism; equivalently the unit $\eta_g:\underline E_Y\to g_*g^{-1}\underline E_Y$ is an isomorphism.
2. For the inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ of a nonempty open subscheme, $c_j:\underline E_Y\to j_*\underline E_U$ is an isomorphism; equivalently the unit $\eta_j:\underline E_Y\to j_*j^{-1}\underline E_Y$ is an isomorphism.

(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.73.13, Tag [09Z5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z5); Stacks states it for any set $E$.*)

proof.text: *The canonical maps and the units.* For $f:Z\to Y$ the map $c_f$ exists and is unique by the adjunction between the constant sheaf and global sections [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections], applied on $Y_{\Et}$ to $\mathcal F=f_*\underline E_Z$, whose global sections are $\underline E_Z(Y\times_YZ)=\underline E_Z(Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The isomorphism $\gamma_f:f^{-1}\underline E_Y\to\underline E_Z$ of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] is the unique isomorphism between the two left adjoints $M\mapsto f^{-1}\underline M_Y$ and $M\mapsto\underline M_Z$ of $\mathcal G\mapsto\Gamma(Z,\mathcal G)=\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal G)$ compatible with their units; the unit of the first is $e\mapsto\eta_f(\iota_Y(e))$, that of the second $e\mapsto\iota_Z(e)$, so $\Gamma(Y,f_*\gamma_f)\circ\eta_f(Y)\circ\iota_Y=\iota_Z$, and by the uniqueness in the constant-sheaf adjunction $f_*(\gamma_f)\circ\eta_f=c_f$. As $\gamma_f$ is an isomorphism, so is $f_*(\gamma_f)$, hence $c_f$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\eta_f$ is. It therefore suffices to prove that $c_g$ and $c_j$ are isomorphisms.

*$g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.* The preimage under $g$ of any open subset of $Y$ is empty or all of the one-point space $\operatorname{Spec}K$, hence quasi-compact; so $g$ is quasi-compact. $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is affine, hence quasi-separated, so $g$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1). (This is the hypothesis of the stalk formula, Stacks Tag 03Q9, which the source cites as Theorem 'higher-direct-images'.)

*The local ring at a geometric point.* Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] lying over $y\in Y$. Choose an affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$ containing $y$; it is nonempty, so it contains the generic point $\eta$ of the irreducible space $Y$, and $A$ is an integral domain [def-pc-integral-scheme] whose zero ideal is the point $\eta$, so $K=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}=A_{(0)}$ is the field of fractions of $A$. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ the localization $A_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], i.e. $A$ is a normal ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] (2) and (3), the strict henselization $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] is canonically the colimit $\varinjlim_{(B,\mathfrak q,\phi)}B$ over the category of triples over $(A,\mathfrak p_y)$, compatibly with the maps from the affine pointed etale neighbourhoods factoring through $V_0$; by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] (1) and (2) this is a filtered colimit of $A$-algebras $B$ etale over $A$, and $C$ is a local ring. In particular $C$ is an $A$-algebra and the canonical morphism $Y_{(\bar y)}=\operatorname{Spec}C\to Y$ is $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A=V_0\subset Y$.

*$\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ is a normal domain.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain], applied to the normal domain $A$ and the local filtered colimit $C$ of etale $A$-algebras of the previous step, $C$ is a normal domain and every nonzero element of $A$ has nonzero image in $C$. (Stacks cites More on Algebra, Lemma 06DI for this.)

*The generic fibre of $Y_{(\bar y)}$ is irreducible.* Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YY_{(\bar y)}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $p:T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Both $g$ and $Y_{(\bar y)}\to Y$ factor through the open subscheme $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ (step 3; $\eta\in V_0$), and an open immersion is a monomorphism, so $T=\operatorname{Spec}K\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}C=\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_AC)$. By step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible] (with $C$ a domain and $A\to C$ injective), $K\otimes_AC$ is a localization of $C$, an integral domain, and $T$ is nonempty, irreducible and connected. (The source: 'Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(K)\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{sh}_{X,\bar x})$ is irreducible.')

*The stalk of $g_*\underline E$ at $\bar y$.* The sheaf $\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ is torsion ($E$ is finite) [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (step 2), so [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] in degree $q=0$ (where $R^0g_*=g_*$, $g_*$ being left exact [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]) gives an isomorphism $\Phi:(g_*\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K})_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T,p^{-1}\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K})$; it sends the class at a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of a section $s\in(g_*\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K})(W)=\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K}(\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YW)$ to the pullback of $s$ along the projection $T\to\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YW$. Composing with $\Gamma(T,\gamma_p)$, $\gamma_p:p^{-1}\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\cong\underline E_T$ [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], identifies the stalk with $\underline E_T(T)$; by the description of $\gamma_p$ in step 1 (its unit sends $e$ to $\iota_T(e)$) and the naturality of $\gamma$ in the base, the pullback of a constant section $\iota_{Z}(e)$ ($Z$ any etale $\operatorname{Spec}K$-scheme) to $T$ goes to $\iota_T(e)$.

*$c_g$ is bijective on the stalk at $\bar y$.* Consider $E\xrightarrow{\epsilon}(\underline E_Y)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{(c_g)_{\bar y}}(g_*\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K})_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\Gamma(T,\gamma_p)\circ\Phi}\underline E_T(T)$, where $\epsilon(e)$ is the class of $\iota_Y(e)$ at $(Y,\bar y)$, an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]. By the definition of $c_g$ (step 1) and its naturality, $c_g(Y)(\iota_Y(e))=\iota_{\operatorname{Spec}K}(e)$, and by step 6 its image in $\underline E_T(T)$ is $\iota_T(e)$; so the composite is $\iota_T$. Since $T$ is connected (step 5), $\iota_T$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected]. As the outer maps $\epsilon$ and $\Gamma(T,\gamma_p)\circ\Phi$ are isomorphisms, $(c_g)_{\bar y}$ is an isomorphism. (Source: 'It follows that the stalk $(g_*\underline E)_{\bar x}$ is equal to $E$'.)

*Conclusion of (1).* The geometric point $\bar y$ was arbitrary, so $c_g$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk and hence an isomorphism of abelian sheaves by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]; by step 1 the unit $\eta_g$ is an isomorphism as well.

*Proof of (2).* Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be a nonempty open. $U$ is an integral normal scheme with the same generic point $\eta$ and function field $K$ (a nonempty open of an irreducible space is irreducible and dense, its affine opens are affine opens of $Y$, and its local rings are those of $Y$) [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], and $g=j\circ g'$ with $g':\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$ the inclusion of its generic point. Let $d=d_{j,g'}:g_*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_*g'_*$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (1). The morphism $j_*(c_{g'})\circ c_j:\underline E_Y\to j_*\underline E_U\to j_*g'_*\underline E_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ sends $\iota_Y(e)$ to $j_*(c_{g'})(\iota_U(e))=\iota_{\operatorname{Spec}K}(e)$, as does $d\circ c_g$ (the component of $d$ at $Y$ is induced by the identification $(Y\times_YU)\times_U\operatorname{Spec}K=\operatorname{Spec}K$); by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections], $j_*(c_{g'})\circ c_j=d\circ c_g$. By (1) for $Y$, $d\circ c_g$ is an isomorphism; by (1) for $U$, $c_{g'}$ and hence $j_*(c_{g'})$ are isomorphisms. Therefore $c_j=j_*(c_{g'})^{-1}\circ d\circ c_g$ is an isomorphism, and so is $\eta_j$ by step 1. (Stacks argues: the map $j_*\underline E\to g_*\underline E$ is injective because $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_YV$ is dense in $U\times_YV$ for every etale $V\to Y$, and $\underline E\to j_*\underline E\to g_*\underline E$ is an isomorphism by (1). Here that map, $d^{-1}\circ j_*(c_{g'})$, is even an isomorphism by (1) applied to $U$, which makes the density argument unnecessary; the structure of the argument is the source's.)
